text_blocks.snippet: Opsumit (macitentan) is a prescription medication used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). It can cause a range of common and serious side effects.

list.snippet: Respiratory and Cold Symptoms: Stuffy or runny nose, sore throat (nasopharyngitis), and bronchitis.
Headaches: Frequent or recurring head pain.
Anemia: Low red blood cell count, which can cause pale skin, tiredness, or weakness.
Infections: Urinary tract infections and flu-like illnesses.
Fluid Retention (Edema): Swelling in the hands, legs, ankles, or feet, typically occurring during the first few weeks of treatment.
Embryo-Fetal Toxicity / Birth Defects: Opsumit causes severe birth defects if taken during pregnancy and is strictly contraindicated for pregnant individuals.
Liver Damage: Elevated liver enzymes or liver injury can occur; symptoms include yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, upper right stomach pain, and severe fatigue.
Severe Fluid Retention & Pulmonary Edema: Rapid weight gain, swelling of the face or limbs, or trouble breathing (sometimes with pink frothy sputum).
Decreased Sperm Count: May impair male fertility by reducing sperm counts.

text_blocks.snippet: More detailed safety and prescribing information is available through the Official Opsumit Website or the FDA Drug Label.
